scope: app_backend.py, main.py, static/, sensorflow/{evaluation,megaeval,safety,seqeval,rca,raremine,bevfusion,vitis,metrics,schemas,adapters} + sensorflow root modules. In-flight namespaces (agentic, nextgen, hillclimb, retro, studio_ux) were READ for context but not audited for fixes.

findings.existing_approach: A hard-coded list `_CA_INTERSECTIONS` of ~110 invented intersections with invented TTC/PET/speed values is served by /api/ssam/statewide as the 'California Statewide SSAM Intersection Safety Dataset', and DATASET_METADATA_STORE claims FHWA public-domain provenance, '845 rows, 100% ingested'.
findings.problem: Fabricated data presented as a real federal safety dataset with false provenance claims. Any downstream consumer (severity ranking, map, annotations) is building on fiction with no simulation marker.
findings.correct_approach: Label every synthetic payload with an explicit provenance field (e.g. data_provenance: SYNTHETIC_ILLUSTRATIVE), remove the FHWA provenance claim or gate it behind an actual ingest, and drive severity from the versioned config in sensorflow/hardening/safety_config.py.
findings.disposition_reason: app_backend.py is under a one-additive-edit budget while five agents are in flight; the extracted, provenance-labeled severity/threshold config is implemented now in sensorflow/hardening/safety_config.py so the wiring change is a one-line import when the file unfreezes.

findings.existing_approach: /api/nvidia/load responds 'Successfully ingested nvidia/PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles samples from HF' while serving hard-coded Unsplash stock photo URLs, invented telemetry and invented chain-of-causation traces (NVIDIA_SAMPLES). The HfApi call is decorative (result discarded, exception swallowed).
findings.problem: The API affirmatively lies about ingestion. A user cannot distinguish this from a real dataset load; annotations saved against it inherit false lineage.
findings.correct_approach: Return status: 'mock' with an explicit simulated flag and provenance enum (see hardening/contracts.py LabelProvenance), or actually ingest.

findings.existing_approach: Association cost adds a 'velocity penalty' computed as `yaw_diff = abs(track.state[2] if len(track.state) > 2 else 0 - prop.bbox_3d[6])`.
findings.problem: Operator-precedence bug: because the Kalman state is [x, y, vx, vy] (len 4 > 2), the expression always evaluates to abs(vx) — the track's forward velocity — not a yaw difference. The 'yaw penalty' is physically meaningless: it penalizes fast-moving objects regardless of orientation, corrupts Hungarian costs, and is compared against a distance gate in meters.
findings.correct_approach: Compute a wrapped angular difference between the track's last observed box yaw and the proposal yaw (the state carries no yaw), and document the penalty's units.
findings.fix: temporal_tracker._associate now computes the wrapped yaw difference from the last observed history box; regression test pins it.

findings.existing_approach: When SAM is unavailable, _fallback_masks builds proposal masks directly from ground-truth boxes, and _assign_taxonomy copies GT class names onto proposals by list index. QualityGate then benchmarks those proposals against the very same GT and the launch gate blocks/permits export on the result.
findings.problem: Circular evaluation: predictions are derived from the reference they are scored against, so quality-gate metrics are inflated and the export gate can pass on leaked information. Class assignment by index conflates MODEL_PREDICTION with AUTO_LABEL-from-GT provenance.
findings.correct_approach: Proposals must carry provenance (LabelProvenance enum); anything derived from GT must be marked and excluded from gate metrics, or the gate must refuse to certify a run whose proposals are GT-derived.
findings.disposition_reason: Removing the GT fallback changes the public demo contract (pipelines without SAM would emit nothing) and shifts every downstream metric; needs a coordinated change with in-flight consumers. Provenance contracts + adapters shipped now in hardening/contracts.py; determinism half of the finding fixed now (F-008).

findings.existing_approach: When training-log parsing yields no losses, /api/train/status fabricates a 'dummy decreasing loss' curve and returns it in the same field as real parsed losses.
findings.problem: The UI cannot distinguish a real converging run from a parser miss; a diverging run whose logs failed to parse renders as a healthy descending curve.
findings.correct_approach: Return an empty list plus a parse_status field; never synthesize values into a field that otherwise carries measurements.

findings.existing_approach: QueryCache.key hashes (population_id, model_version, filters, group_by, metrics). The router cache is shared across all runs in the MegaStore.
findings.problem: The key omits run identity: label_version, threshold_config, parameter overrides and seed all live in run.lineage and all change results. Two runs with the same population+model but different overrides (e.g. an injected regression) collide — queries for run B can silently return run A's cached rows.
findings.correct_approach: Key the cache on the immutable run_id (which pins the full lineage) plus query shape; in a multi-node deployment add evaluator_code_version and metric_version.
findings.fix: QueryRouter.query now scopes the key with run.run_id (API-preserving; QueryCache.key signature unchanged). Test pins that two runs with different overrides no longer share cache entries.

findings.existing_approach: _compute_severity buries magic weights (0.5/0.2/0.3), caps (TTC 1.5s / PET 5.0s / speed 18 m/s) and band cutoffs (0.7/0.45/0.25) as literals; the legacy /api/ssam/streets endpoint uses a DIFFERENT weighting (0.7/0.3) for the same severity concept; rare_events.py hard-codes TTC<3.0/1.8 and PET<1.5 corridor literals.
findings.problem: Safety-relevant constants have no provenance, no version, and are inconsistent between two endpoints computing 'the same' severity — the same intersection gets two severities depending on the route called.
findings.correct_approach: Single versioned threshold registry with per-parameter provenance labels (FHWA_SSAM_DEFAULT vs ILLUSTRATIVE_THRESHOLD), consumed by both endpoints.
findings.disposition_reason: Registry implemented now (sensorflow/hardening/safety_config.py) with every legacy literal captured and labeled; rewiring app_backend.py is a documented follow-up under the edit budget.

findings.existing_approach: _load_lidar silently substitutes `np.random.randn(500, 3) * 2` — unseeded — when the LiDAR file is missing.
findings.problem: Unseeded randomness in a production labeling path: two identical runs produce different proposals, and the fake point cloud carries no synthetic marker.
findings.correct_approach: Deterministic seed derived from the file path; explicit SYNTHETIC_FALLBACK labeling in code and docstring.
findings.fix: Seeded per-path RNG (stable hash), documented as a synthetic fallback. Test pins determinism.

findings.existing_approach: _collect_boxes pools every predicted box and every GT box across ALL frames into two flat lists before matching; compute_map_mar and _match_for_errors then match across the pooled lists.
findings.problem: A prediction in frame 1 may match a GT box in frame 50 if their coordinates coincide. On any multi-frame sequence the reported mAP/mAR/mean-IoU/position error are computed over physically impossible matches, and the launch gate consumes these numbers.
findings.correct_approach: Match per frame; aggregate TP/FP/FN and matched-pair errors across frames.
findings.fix: QualityGate now groups boxes by frame_id and matches within frames only (evaluate() signature and result shape unchanged). Test pins that cross-frame coincidences no longer match.

findings.existing_approach: compare_runs flags a regression whenever a point-estimate delta exceeds a fixed tolerance (e.g. recall drop > 0.03). No sample sizes, no confidence intervals, no power, no multiple-testing policy across the 9 metrics tested.
findings.problem: On small runs a 3pp delta is noise (a 500-object run has ~±4pp Wilson width at p=0.9); on huge runs a real 2.9pp regression is silently ignored. Nine metrics tested independently inflates false-alarm probability. This is exactly the class of naive comparison seqeval was built to replace.
findings.correct_approach: Proportion deltas should use CI-aware decisions (Wilson two-proportion or seqeval's paired anytime-valid test) with the tolerance acting as a practical-significance margin; multiple metrics need a family-wise policy (seqeval ships e-BH).
findings.fix: compare_runs gained an optional, API-preserving `sample_sizes` argument: when counts are provided for a proportion metric, the regression flag requires the Wilson CI of the delta to exclude the tolerance band (delta_ci recorded on the RegressionMetricDelta). Default behavior without counts is unchanged. Full seqeval delegation for the pipeline path is a documented follow-up.

findings.existing_approach: After every run, the current run's metrics overwrite store.meta['baseline_metrics']; each run is compared only to the immediately preceding run.
findings.problem: Rolling baseline: a model can regress 1pp per run for ten runs and never trip the 3pp tolerance — classic slow-drift masking.
findings.correct_approach: Pin the baseline to a released/blessed run; compare against pinned baseline AND previous run; alert on cumulative drift.
findings.disposition_reason: Changing baseline semantics alters the public behavior of every subsequent pipeline run; needs a product decision on which run is 'blessed'. Documented with proposed pinned-baseline design.

findings.existing_approach: Five grader sources vote; consensus = reliability-weighted majority share (weights 2.0/1.0/0.75/0.75/0.5 — arbitrary) blended 0.5/0.35/0.15 with spatial/temporal agreement. Grader errors are simulated independently per grader.
findings.problem: Consensus treats graders as independent evidence. In reality historical_model, vlm_label and independent_detector may share training data, backbones, or sensor blind spots; agreement among correlated graders is worth far less than the naive consensus implies. There is no dependence discount anywhere.
findings.correct_approach: Model pairwise grader dependence (shared backbone/data/architecture) and compute an independence-adjusted effective grader count alongside naive consensus; route on the adjusted value.
findings.fix: sensorflow/hardening/quality.py implements a grader-dependence model (shared-resource dependence matrix -> effective number of independent graders -> adjusted confidence) layered on top of graders.py without modifying it; tests pin that correlated panels always score below naive consensus.

findings.existing_approach: /api/yaml/content reads and /api/yaml/save writes ANY absolute or relative filesystem path supplied by the client.
findings.problem: Arbitrary file read/write from an unauthenticated HTTP endpoint (path traversal by design). Acceptable only on a loopback dev box; disqualifying anywhere else.
findings.correct_approach: Allowlist a config directory, resolve+verify the path prefix, reject absolute paths.

findings.existing_approach: The accident-analysis gateway runs Mock* classes that return constant fabricated values (quality_score 0.95, risk_index 0.75, confidence_score 0.89, hard-coded hotspots) and reports 'status: success' with `processing_time_seconds: len(clean_df)` (row count masquerading as seconds).
findings.problem: Class names say Mock internally but the API response carries no simulation marker — callers receive fabricated risk indices as if computed, plus a nonsense processing-time value.
findings.correct_approach: Additive `simulated: true` + `analysis_provenance` markers on every response built from mock engines; measure actual elapsed time.
findings.fix: main.py responses now carry simulated/analysis_provenance markers and a real measured processing_time_seconds (additive fields; existing fields unchanged).

findings.existing_approach: Triage decisions are explainable (per-gate lines — a genuine strength), but everything FLAGGED lands in a flat FIFO review batch with no prioritization; mitl_copilot routes on 3 duplicated thresholds and attaches `pred_tracks[:3]` (the first three tracks, unrelated to the failure) as 'evidence'; severities are hard-coded strings.
findings.problem: Review effort is not allocated by information value: a near-miss VRU ambiguity queues behind a low-stakes dimension quibble. No acceptance metrics exist for the routing itself (HITL precision, critical-miss-rate, workload), so the queue can silently degrade.
findings.correct_approach: Score each flagged item by Risk x Uncertainty x Novelty x TrainingValue (or Pareto rank on the components); track HITL precision/recall/workload/critical-miss-rate/false-routing-rate as first-class metrics.
findings.fix: sensorflow/hardening/hitl.py implements both prioritizers with a documented comparison and the acceptance-metric calculator; wiring the labeleval review queue through it is a follow-up (queue semantics owned by evaluation package consumers).

findings.existing_approach: Kalman process noise Q = 0.1*I and measurement noise R = 0.5*I, identical across position and velocity states.
findings.problem: Uncalibrated, unitless noise constants with no provenance; velocity noise in (m/s)^2 sharing a scalar with position noise in m^2 is physically incoherent.
findings.correct_approach: Derive Q from an assumed acceleration noise (white-noise-acceleration model) and R from sensor spec; expose as config.

findings.existing_approach: quality_score = map*40 + (1-orient/45)*20 + (1-swap/0.1)*20 + (1-frag/0.2)*20; error matching uses greedy IoU>0.3.
findings.problem: Magic weights and denominators with no documented rationale produce a headline '0-100 quality score' that looks authoritative but is arbitrary.
findings.correct_approach: Keep the decomposed metric card authoritative; if a scalar is needed, document the weighting as ILLUSTRATIVE and version it.

findings.existing_approach: compute_map_mar reports 'mAP' that is actually precision at fixed IoU thresholds — no confidence ranking, no PR curve integration; also recomputes the full matching three times.
findings.problem: Metric misnomer: consumers comparing this 'mAP' against literature mAP will draw wrong conclusions.
findings.correct_approach: Rename or document as precision@IoU; implement ranked AP if mAP is required.
findings.fix: Docstring corrected to state exactly what is computed (non-breaking); the rename is an API-breaking follow-up.

findings.existing_approach: ID-swap attribution matches each GT frame to the nearest predicted box with NO distance gate.
findings.problem: A predicted track 500m away 'matches' a GT instance if it is merely the nearest, manufacturing phantom ID swaps (or hiding real ones) on sparse scenes.
findings.correct_approach: Gate the match at the same threshold fragmentation already uses (2.0 m default).
findings.fix: compute_id_swap_rate gained match_threshold_m (default 2.0, matching fragmentation) applied to candidate matches; API-preserving keyword.

findings.existing_approach: rarity = clip(1 - freq*4, 0.05, 1) and confidence = clip(0.55 + 0.4*rarity, 0, 0.99).
findings.problem: The '4' is arbitrary; worse, 'confidence' is fabricated FROM rarity — a rare event is automatically a confident detection, which inverts how evidence works. It is not a placeholder-free novelty score (no kNN/density/embedding basis).
findings.correct_approach: Rarity from inverse frequency is fine if documented; confidence must derive from evidence strength (sensor count, anomaly score), not rarity. Real novelty scoring (kNN + centroid distance) implemented in sensorflow/hardening/sampling.py.
findings.disposition_reason: Changing RareEvent.confidence semantics alters persisted records consumed by the UI; hardening/sampling.py provides the corrected scorer for adoption.

findings.existing_approach: If a detector raises during fit/score, its scores are silently replaced with zeros and still averaged into the ensemble.
findings.problem: Silent degradation: a crashed detector drags every ensemble score toward 'normal' (rank-normalized zeros), masking anomalies with no operator signal.
findings.correct_approach: Record and expose per-detector failures; exclude failed detectors from the ensemble average.
findings.fix: AnomalyEnsemble.run now records failures in self.failures, excludes failed detectors from the combination, and keeps the return signature unchanged.

findings.existing_approach: When seqeval is unavailable, a paired-t CI on per-frame mean correctness deltas produces the verdict; documented as not anytime-valid.
findings.problem: Frames within a sequence are temporally correlated, so frame-level SEM understates variance (no sequence-level clustering); honest labeling mitigates but does not remove the risk.
findings.correct_approach: Cluster deltas at sequence level before the t-interval (mirroring seqeval's cluster-mean design).
findings.disposition_reason: Fallback path only (seqeval is importable in this repo, so the fallback is dormant); low blast radius.

findings.existing_approach: A personal Tailscale hostname (dgx-spark.tail16d8d9.ts.net) is hard-coded as the primary LLM endpoint in three places.
findings.problem: Environment-specific infrastructure baked into source; both an information leak and a portability failure.
findings.correct_approach: Environment-variable override with localhost default.
findings.fix: mitl_copilot.py endpoints are now env-overridable (SENSORFLOW_OLLAMA_URL/MODEL) with unchanged defaults; the app_backend.py occurrences are follow-ups under the edit budget.

findings.existing_approach: ground_contact_error assumes a global flat ground plane at z=0.
findings.problem: On sloped/banked roads the check produces physically meaningless penalties; threshold 0.5m is a synthetic-world constant.
findings.correct_approach: Use local ground estimate (e.g. lowest LiDAR percentile near the object) as reference.

findings.existing_approach: CORS allow_origins=['*'] combined with allow_credentials=True.
findings.problem: Credentials + wildcard origin is a disallowed combination (browsers reject it, and if origin-echo middleware were added it would become a CSRF vector).
findings.correct_approach: Explicit origin allowlist; drop credentials if wildcard is required.
findings.disposition_reason: Behavioral change to a standalone demo app's cross-origin contract; documented.

findings.existing_approach: All stores are JSON/npz files under runs/ plus in-process singletons; app_backend holds training state in module globals; megaeval narrates Spark-executor semantics while running threads on one node.
findings.problem: The aggregate-first architecture is genuinely scale-shaped (a strength), but there is no storage/compute interface seam: nothing separates 'local demo store' from 'production store', so every store is silently single-node, single-process, lost-on-restart.
findings.correct_approach: Interface protocols (VectorDB, ObjectStorage, DistributedCompute, GPUInference, FeatureCache, MetadataStore, ExperimentTracking, Observability) with the current implementations registered as explicitly-labeled LOCAL/MOCK.
findings.fix: sensorflow/hardening/interfaces.py defines the eight protocols with local implementations registered and labeled LOCAL, and docstrings naming production options.

findings.existing_approach: MegaStore._artifacts evicts the oldest-inserted entry when >6 cached run artifact sets.
findings.problem: Insertion-order eviction (not LRU) can evict the hot run; no integrity check on npz artifacts (a truncated file loads as a crash, not a checksum failure).
findings.correct_approach: LRU + artifact checksums; see hardening/cache_manifest.py for the manifest design.

findings.existing_approach: /api/benchmark/compare falls back to invented per-model metrics but does label the payload source: 'fallback_mock'.
findings.problem: The label is good practice; the invented numbers (latencies, recalls for named public models) still risk being quoted.
findings.correct_approach: Keep the label; replace invented numbers with nulls + descriptions.

findings.existing_approach: Stratified risk-weighted review sampling with true population weights (classic stratified estimator) and Wilson per-stratum CIs; simulated reviewers at HUMAN_FIDELITY=0.985 (documented).
findings.problem: VERIFIED CORRECT: over-sampling risky strata is undone by W_h weighting, so estimates are honest (the reweighting the audit was told to verify). Residual caveats: _allocate's max(1, ...) rounding can overshoot target_n slightly, and reviewer error (1.5%) is not deconvolved from the estimate.
findings.correct_approach: Optionally largest-remainder allocation and Rogan-Gladen correction for reviewer error.

findings.existing_approach: Optional meta_classifier ensemble strategy is supervised by injected_errors — the synthetic generator's own error labels — with a held-out split.
findings.problem: Held-out split avoids memorization, but the supervision signal only exists for synthetic data; if this strategy were enabled on real data the code path would silently have no labels. Default strategy is weighted_average, so dormant.
findings.correct_approach: Guard the strategy behind an explicit synthetic-data check.

strengths.what: Anytime-valid sequential testing done properly: empirical-Bernstein confidence sequences, betting e-processes with Ville's inequality, three-outcome decisions against a practical margin, cluster-mean inputs for correlation, e-BH for multiplicity. This is the statistical gold standard in the repo — regression.py and vitis/hil.py fallbacks should delegate here.
strengths.reuse: power.py in the hardening package delegates all sequential sizing to seqeval; hil.py already prefers it.

strengths.what: Correct stratified estimation (risk-weighted allocation with true-weight recombination, Wilson CIs) and a complete lineage record (dataset/model/label/evaluator/metric versions, threshold config, seed, hardware) on every run. The aggregate-first cube with honest scan fallback is the right architecture for scale.
strengths.reuse: hardening/sampling.py reuses the W_h recombination pattern; the lineage field set seeds the FeatureCacheEntry manifest design.

strengths.what: The leakage guard is real: protected eval destinations force training_eligible=False, promotion of protected examples raises LeakageError absent an audited governance override, unvalidated candidates can never route to training. Modality discipline is hard-enforced (evidence from absent modalities raises).
strengths.reuse: hardening/contracts.py provenance rules mirror this guard; the audit verified evaluation/synthetic and megaeval paths cannot cross it because they never construct raremine destinations.

strengths.what: Cluster-robust paired deltas with ICC/design-effect effective n, PSI with practical-effect labels, three-way CI outcomes. Explicitly defers to seqeval for sequential use.
strengths.reuse: hardening/power.py reuses the design-effect formulation for pairing/clustering corrections.

strengths.what: Honest labeling done right: FHWA-defaulted thresholds carry provenance comments, synthetic trajectories and the reaction-time mapping are explicitly marked simulated ('not a physics-validated driver model'), and TTC/PET use real geometry (support functions, zone-grid occupancy).
strengths.reuse: safety_config.py adopts its provenance-comment convention as the ILLUSTRATIVE_THRESHOLD pattern.

strengths.what: Every modeled number carries 'modeled_not_measured: True'; the hardware backend is an explicit non-constructible stub; the HIL verdict prefers seqeval and labels its fallback.
strengths.reuse: interfaces.py LOCAL/MOCK labeling convention follows this pattern.

strengths.what: Triage decisions store per-gate actual-vs-threshold lines with policy id/values (real explainability); anomaly detection uses genuine kNN/LOF/IsolationForest/OCSVM implementations, seeded, with honest 'numpy stand-in' labels on the deep detectors; Cohen/Fleiss/Krippendorff are used in their correct regimes.
strengths.reuse: hardening/quality.py routing keeps this decomposed-gates style and layers dependence adjustment on top.
